ref_issue.title: Send SIGTERM before SIGKILL when cancelling host-mode jobs
ref_issue.body:
### How to use this feature request

* Please describe your first hand experience in a comment to show why you are interested into the same feature.
* Please don't comment if you have no relevant information to add. It's just extra noise for everyone subscribed to this issue.
* Subscribe to receive notifications on status change and new comments.

### First hand experience

- I ran a workflow on Codeberg that starts an AWS CodeBuild build and streams its logs back to the Actions UI.
- I cancelled the workflow. The Actions job was cancelled, but the AWS CodeBuild build continued running.
- I configured the AWS action to handle both `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`, then repeated the test. The build still continued and eventually succeeded.
- Investigating Forgejo Runner’s code showed that cancellation sends `SIGKILL`, preventing the action’s signal handlers from requesting that AWS CodeBuild stop.
- I now have to stop the AWS build separately when cancelling the workflow.
- [Issue #1792](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/issues/1792) reports another consequence of this behavior: Git cannot remove its lock file, breaking subsequent jobs until manual cleanup.


My experimentation is here: https://codeberg.org/alex6/gitea-actions-examples

### Needs and benefits

- Allow processes to clean up before forced termination.
- Let actions stop external workloads, avoiding unnecessary resource usage and costs.
- Give tools such as Git an opportunity to remove temporary lock files, as described in
  [issue #1792](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/issues/1792).

### Feature Description

- Use staged termination when cancelling runner-managed processes: send `SIGINT`, allow a bounded grace period,
  then escalate to `SIGTERM` and finally `SIGKILL` if processes remain.
- Apply this to action execution and runner-managed subprocesses such as action fetching.
- Replace immediate `SIGKILL` with a bounded opportunity for graceful cleanup while ensuring cancellation
  completes even when processes do not cooperate.

### What needs to happen before a feature request is ready to be implemented?

Users can complete the first step (accumulating first and experience) on their own, even if this feature request did not catch the eye of someone with the necessary skills to implement it. And when it reaches that point, it will stand out and have a much higher chance of being implemented. 

1. **A few other users contributed their own first hand experience.**
   To fully grasp the scope of a feature request, and to brainstorm possible solutions, a feature request will generally wait until several users have provided their perspective.
   Thumbs-up reactions help gauge popularity, but do not provide the same amount of useful information.
1. **The "Needs and benefit" and "Feature description" are finalized.**
   Results from discussions and additional user experiences are incorporated into a final summary to provide a single reference for the developers working on this change.
   This can be done by the author of the issue or anyone else in a followup comment.
1. **The label `Stage/Idea` is changed to `Stage/Ready`.**
1. **Feature request is created in the repository where the code resides.**
   Depending on the feature request it can be in [Forgejo](https://codeberg.org/orbit/orbit/issues/new?template=.forgejo%2fissue_template%2ffeature-request.yaml) or [Forgejo runner](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/issues/new?template=.forgejo%2fissue_template%2ffeature-request.yaml).
   A copy/paste of the "Needs and benefit" and "Feature description" should be used, with link to this issue so the developer knows where to find more details if they need to.
